situation.problem_text:
Topic: Mastering the Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

Target audience: University students (Engineering or Mathematics)

Section: section_1 — Intuitive Hook: The Observer's Perspective

Lecture lines:
Coordinates are relative to an observer.
A robot finds a box's location.
Changing the grid alters the description.
Physical location remains constant.
Language changes, reality stays the same.

Planned animations:
Display a vector 'v' in a coordinate system with basis {e1, e2} (color #FFFFFF).
Show another basis {b1, b2} (color #FFFF00) as alternative perspective.
Highlight the vector 'v' as independent of the chosen basis.
Show 'v' decomposed into {e1, e2} coordinates.
Show 'v' decomposed into {b1, b2} coordinates.

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite Review: Basis as Building Blocks

Lecture lines:
A basis is our building block.
Vectors must be linearly independent.
Standard basis uses cardinal directions.

Planned animations:
Display the standard basis vectors i, j (color #FFFFFF).
Form a grid using i, j as the basis.
Introduce a new basis {b1, b2} (color #00FF00) as vectors.

Section: section_3 — The Change of Basis Matrix (The 'Translator')

Lecture lines:
Need a translator between bases.
Columns are the new basis vectors.
Matrix P connects different grid overlays.
Convert [v]_B to [v]_A.
Compute [v]_A equals P times [v]_B.

Planned animations:
Place basis vectors b1, b2 into matrix columns (color #00FFFF).
Show the matrix multiplying coordinate vector [c1, c2].
Reveal the output as the original vector in standard basis.
Animate the transformation of the grid from {e1, e2} to {b1, b2}.
Label this process as 'Change of Basis'.

Section: section_4 — Visualizing the Inverse

Lecture lines:
How do we reverse the translation?
P-inverse takes us back to A.
Grid stretches and shears together.

Planned animations:
Show the Change of Basis matrix (color #00FFFF).
Highlight the inverse matrix (color #FF00FF).
Demonstrate multiplying by inverse to undo the basis change.

Section: section_5 — Summary and Conclusion

Lecture lines:
Change of basis is just language.
Simplifies complex physics and engineering.
Choosing the right basis helps.

Planned animations:
Summarize the core concept: Change of Basis as perspective shift.
Display both coordinate sets next to the invariant vector.
Conclude with the importance of translation between frames.

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
